Chapter 6 The Unexpected Gifts of Struggle.
You know, sometimes the toughest days end up leaving us with the most surprising gifts. Not the kind of gift anyone would wish for—nobody wakes up hoping to feel anxious, or to carry the heavy weight of depression. But over time, people who face these challenges often find themselves holding onto a unique wisdom, a deeper empathy, and a sharper appreciation for life’s simple, good things.
Imagine sitting in a waiting room. Your heart’s pounding, palms sweaty, and you’re absolutely convinced that everyone around you notices your discomfort. Every part of you wants to get up and run, but you stay. Then, a stranger sits down beside you—clearly nervous. Without even thinking, you offer a quiet word of reassurance. The stranger visibly relaxes, and suddenly, your anxiety doesn’t feel quite so isolating. In that moment, it feels less like a curse and more like a bridge between two people.
Most folks don’t realize just how much strength it takes to keep showing up when everything inside you says to hide. But if you’ve been there—and you keep going, even when it’s hard—you start to notice something. You become more tuned in to the struggles of others. It’s as if pain, though nobody invites it in, can actually open the door to compassion.
Picture a teacher who’s spent years wrestling with their own mental health. One day, they notice a student slowly withdrawing from class. Instead of ignoring it—or getting frustrated—they gently check in. The student’s relief is obvious. It’s just a small gesture, but it means the world. The teacher’s own struggles have made them more patient, more willing to listen.
And as the years pass, these unexpected gifts of struggle become clearer. There’s a deeper appreciation for laughter, for those quiet, peaceful moments, and for the rare days when things just feel okay. After a storm, the world’s colors can look a little brighter. It becomes obvious that, while no one would ever choose pain, it can shape us in ways that are both unexpected and genuinely beautiful.
Living with mental illness is never easy. But it can help grow resilience, empathy, and a fierce determination to find joy—even on the darkest days. And these are the gifts that don’t come in spite of the struggle, but because of it.
